00327.label: Continuous daily sunitinib · pancreatic NET
additional_support: Use the unit’s gentle skin and mouth-care plan. Report hand-foot pain before it limits walking or daily tasks; the team may adjust treatment.
This oral regimen is minimal-to-low emetogenic. Routine premedication is not required. Agree rescue anti-sickness and antidiarrhoeal medicines and when to call.
Follow the agreed BP plan. If you use diabetes medicines, ask how to monitor glucose and manage low readings; sunitinib may lower blood sugar.
Report poor intake, weight loss or troublesome fatigue. Thyroid changes, anaemia, dehydration or other causes may need treatment.
No routine premedication is required by NCCP. Any antidiarrhoeal, rescue antiemetic or other support must follow the local prescription.

guidance.label: Use the prescribed local supportive-care plan; independent clinical/pharmacy review pending

00505.label: CAPTEM · capecitabine D1–14 and temozolomide D10–14
00505.emetogenic_risk: Capecitabine oral minimal-to-low; temozolomide oral moderate-to-high
additional_support: Capecitabine is minimal-to-low emetogenic, while temozolomide is moderate-to-high emetogenic in this oral schedule. The team must prescribe an oral anti-sickness plan for Days 10–14 and any rescue treatment; this is not a single low-risk infusion plan.
Use the unit’s mouth and skin care. Significant pain, ulcers or hand-foot symptoms may require capecitabine interruption; do not keep taking tablets just to finish the fortnight.
Ask for written diarrhoea instructions and the point at which to stop capecitabine and call. Persistent vomiting, severe diarrhoea, dizziness or inability to drink needs urgent advice.

The team assesses whether PJP prevention is needed under local policy, especially with steroid exposure or other risk factors. CAPTEM is not the 42-day temozolomide-plus-radiotherapy schedule; do not borrow that schedule’s automatic prevention plan.
A separate prescribed oral antiemetic plan is required for temozolomide Days 10–14. The source does not specify one universal drug/dose; do not substitute a parenteral low-risk bundle.
Day-specific administration: capecitabine with food/within 30 minutes; temozolomide fasting. Omitted toxicity doses are not replaced.
PJP prevention is a local risk-based decision for this five-day temozolomide exposure, not automatic adoption of the 42-day brain radiotherapy regimen.

guidance.label: Use the prescribed local supportive-care plan; independent clinical/pharmacy review pending

00642.label: PRRT administration with kidney protection

medicines.name: 5-HT3 antagonist antiemetic
medicines.dose: Agent and dose prescribed by the nuclear-medicine service
medicines.timing: At least 30 minutes before the amino-acid infusion
medicines.note: NCCP regimen recommendation; additional antiemetics if needed under local policy.

medicines.name: Lysine / arginine amino-acid infusion
medicines.dose: Formulation and volume prescribed by the specialist service
medicines.timing: Start 30 minutes before Lutathera and continue for four hours
medicines.note: Required kidney protection. Check potassium beforehand; fluid/renal/cardiac risk may require an individual plan.

additional_support: A lysine/arginine infusion is required for kidney protection and begins before Lutathera. Follow the service’s fluid and toileting advice. Tell staff about heart or kidney problems; do not use a generic fluid target.

PRRT has moderate emetogenic potential. A 5-HT3 anti-sickness medicine is given at least 30 minutes before the amino-acid infusion, with additional treatment if needed. Tell staff promptly if nausea starts.

Long-acting SSA injections can interfere with receptor targeting. NCCP uses a 30-day interval before PRRT and short-acting injections are withheld for 24 hours. The referring NET consultant decides your exact stop and restart plan, balancing hormone control. Never stop injections on your own.

The medical physicist gives individual written and verbal advice. Contact with young children or pregnant people may need restriction for up to three weeks, and close-contact work may require up to two weeks away. Arrange transport, sleeping, toileting, laundry and caring responsibilities before admission.
Radiation safety: individual medical-physicist instructions and official radiation card; the SACTCheck wallet card does not replace them.
The long Irish leaflet describes earlier additional post-course blood tests and service scan timings; reconcile the written service plan with the NCCP minimum monitoring sequence.
Do not restart SSA injections, prescribe steroids or add electrolyte/fluid treatment without the relevant specialist plan.
